name: NY-22
label: Likely D

key_factors: Both major prediction markets price Mannion near 95 percent to win
Mannion holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising and cash advantage over Buller
The district leans Democratic (D+4) and Mannion has incumbency on his side
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so uncertainty stays elevated
model.rationale: Markets price the incumbent near 95 percent, and Mannion pairs incumbency with an overwhelming financial edge in a district that leans Democratic, leaving Buller little visible path. With no public polling available, the expected margin stays moderate relative to the money gap, respecting the district's modest lean and the market signal rather than an aggressive fundamentals read.
model.watch: Any public polling, expert ratings, or outside spending entering the district could move this estimate quickly.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
John Mannion, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a central New York district that leans about four points Democratic. He holds a commanding financial position, with roughly $2.7 million raised and $1.8 million on hand, against about $267,000 raised and $187,000 on hand for Republican Kailee Buller. No outside groups have reported spending in the race.

No public polls cover the contest and no expert raters track it, so the picture rests on fundamentals and markets. Both major prediction markets price Mannion near 95 percent, marking him as a clear but not overwhelming favorite. Incumbency, the district's Democratic lean, and his money advantage point to a double-digit expected margin, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty wider than in truly safe seats.
